1 · Project Overview

The Private Villa, owned by Engr. Sultan Batterjee, is a prestigious luxury residential development located in Jeddah, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. Constructed and delivered by IHCC (International Hospital Construction Company), the villa represents a benchmark in high-end residential construction, combining architectural elegance with advanced mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) systems.

The interior design concept was developed and executed by Raven & Lack London, bringing a refined international aesthetic to this landmark property. The villa is designed as a fully self-contained private residence, offering exceptional levels of comfort, privacy, security, and functionality across four levels: Basement, Ground Floor, First Floor, and Roof.

3 · Key Building Features
3.1 Vertical Transportation
The villa is equipped with two lifts: a passenger lift serving Ground Floor, First Floor, and the Upper Roof Terrace; and a service lift connecting the Basement, Ground Floor, and Lower Roof for equipment access and maintenance purposes. A car lift connects the Ground Floor garage directly to the Basement parking area.
3.2 Swimming Pools
The villa features two distinct aquatic facilities: an outdoor swimming pool (50 m²) located on the Ground Floor in the landscape area, and a private indoor pool with integrated Jacuzzi located in the Basement wellness zone. A Cold Plunge Pool is also provided within the Basement spa area. All pool systems are served by a dedicated pump room located in the Basement.
3.3 Parking Facilities
A total of 10 car parking spaces are provided across two levels. Three spaces are available on the Ground Floor within the covered garage, and seven additional spaces are provided in the Basement parking area. Both levels are connected via the car lift system.
3.4 Wellness & Spa
The Basement Wellness Zone is a comprehensive private spa designed to international hospitality standards. It includes a sauna, steam room, massage room, cold plunge pool, indoor Jacuzzi, his and her change rooms with showers, and a spa lobby. This facility provides a self-contained wellness experience within the residential environment.
3.5 MEP & Building Services
The villa is equipped with a full suite of mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) systems including HVAC, water supply and drainage, electrical distribution, and solar panels on the roof. All major HVAC equipment is consolidated on the Lower Roof level for ease of maintenance access. Dedicated HVAC shafts, electrical shafts, and toilet vent shafts are provided throughout the building to ensure clean and coordinated service distribution.

02 Plumbing System Overview

The CEO Villa is equipped with a state-of-the-art plumbing infrastructure designed to deliver exceptional water quality, reliable supply, and complete waste removal across all four levels of this luxury private residence. The system is engineered to the highest international standards and serves 42 domestic facilities across the Basement, Ground Floor, First Floor, and Roof, in addition to two swimming pools, a dedicated wellness spa, a full irrigation network, and multiple outdoor areas.

Water enters the villa from the municipality network into a large underground concrete storage tank of 103 m³ capacity. From this point, it is transferred by dedicated pumps through a multi-stage treatment train — sediment filtration, carbon filtration, ion-exchange softening, and UV disinfection — before being pressurized and distributed through a three-pipe network (Cold Water Supply, Hot Water Supply, Hot Water Return) to all fixtures and appliances. Wastewater is removed through a fully separate gravity drainage system, pressurized basement sump pits, and a dedicated rainwater collection and discharge system. All systems work together to provide a seamless, self-sufficient water cycle within the villa.

03 Water Supply System

The water supply system is the backbone of all plumbing services in CEO Villa. It follows a well-defined path from raw municipal supply through storage, treatment, pressurization, and final distribution to every tap, shower, and appliance. The system is designed with full redundancy — dual pumps in duty/standby configuration at every stage — ensuring uninterrupted water service even during maintenance or equipment failure.

3.1 · Main Water Storage Tank

Water is received from the municipality through a 25mm UPVC connection and stored in a large underground concrete tank with a capacity of 103 m³ located on the North-East side of the villa. This tank is the primary water reservoir for the entire building. Access is provided through 800×800mm cast iron covers at the municipality connection, truck filling point, and float valve locations.

ParameterDetail
TypeUnderground Reinforced Concrete
Capacity103 m³ (103,000 Litres)
Primary FillMunicipality water — 25mm UPVC line with 1" float valve (auto shut-off)
Secondary Fill4" UPVC truck fill line with 4" float valve (manual top-up)

3.2 · Water Treatment Train — 4-Stage Process

Under normal operation, water is drawn from the main underground storage tank by the Irrigation Pumps (P-01/P-02). The pump discharge header serves two purposes simultaneously — one branch feeds the Irrigation System, while the other branch feeds the domestic Water Supply System.

Water from the supply branch passes through 4 consecutive treatment stages before being stored in the 2,000L treated water buffer tank. This multi-stage process ensures clean, soft, odour-free, and bacteria-free water is delivered to every fixture in the villa.

The tank level is controlled by a float valve — when the water level drops, the float valve opens, allowing the irrigation pumps to refill the tank automatically. Once the tank reaches full capacity, the float valve closes and the pumps stop. This buffer ensures continuous supply during softener regeneration cycles.

STEP 1
SEDIMENT FILTRATION (SCF-1 & SCF-2) — Dual parallel SHELCO stainless steel cartridge filters (5-micron). Removes sand, rust, silt and suspended solids. Flow: 50 GPM each. Only one runs at a time; second is standby.
STEP 2
ACTIVATED CARBON FILTRATION (CCF-01) — SHELCO carbon cartridge filter removes chlorine, taste, and odour compounds. Protects downstream softener resin from chlorine damage. Replace every 6 months.
STEP 3
WATER SOFTENING (WS-01) — PENTAIR FRP vessel with 4 cu.ft. cation-exchange resin. CLACK WS1 control valve with automatic regeneration. Removes calcium & magnesium (hardness) to <1 GPG. Brine tank 70-100L for salt regeneration.
STEP 4
UV DISINFECTION (UV-01) — LUMINOR RAINIER LR6-553 UV sterilizer. 254nm wavelength achieves 99.99% kill rate for bacteria, viruses, Giardia and Cryptosporidium. No chemical residue. Built-in intensity meter monitors lamp performance.
3.3 · Cold Water Booster Pump System

Treated water is pressurized and distributed throughout the villa by twin LOWARA-Xylem multistage booster pumps operating in duty/standby configuration under VFD (Variable Frequency Drive) control. The VFD maintains constant pressure regardless of demand fluctuation — speeding up during peak use and slowing down during low demand, saving energy and preventing pressure surges.

Cold water is distributed throughout the villa via AQUATHERM PPR (Polypropylene Random Copolymer) pipes — German-made, SDR 7.4 rating, PN-20 pressure class — the premium choice for domestic plumbing. 4.2 · Thermal Disinfection — CALEFFI LEGIOMIX System

Legionella pneumophila bacteria thrive in warm water systems between 20-45°C. Without active control, they can colonize hot water pipes and cause serious health risks. The CALEFFI LEGIOMIX Brain Digital Valve (BDV-01) is the villa's automated defense system against this risk — it mixes hot and cold water to safe delivery temperatures during normal operation and periodically raises the entire hot water system to 65°C to kill any bacteria present.

STEP 1
NORMAL OPERATION — CALEFFI mixes hot (55-65°C from heaters) with cold water, delivering a safe and comfortable 42-48°C to all fixtures. Motorized mixing ball valve adjusts automatically to maintain setpoint within ±3°C.
STEP 2
DISINFECTION TRIGGER — Weekly cycle (typically Sunday 2-4 AM). Controller verifies heater temperature is above 60°C, cold water is available, and circulation flow is adequate before proceeding.
STEP 3
RAMP-UP PHASE (5-10 min) — Valve gradually increases hot proportion. Temperature rises steadily toward 65°C. Controlled to prevent thermal shock to piping.
STEP 4
DISINFECTION HOLD (30 min) — Entire hot water distribution maintained at 65°C. Hot water circulates through all branches and dead legs. Continuous temperature monitoring throughout.
STEP 5
COOL-DOWN PHASE (10-15 min) — Temperature gradually reduced back to normal 42-48°C delivery range. System protection during cooldown prevents sudden thermal changes.
STEP 6
RETURN TO NORMAL — System resumes normal mixing. Hot water available to all fixtures. Disinfection log recorded by controller.
ComponentSpecification

06 Sanitary Drainage System

The sanitary drainage system collects and removes all wastewater generated by 43 drainage points across the villa — toilets, showers, basins, kitchens, laundries, and floor drains. Upper floor waste flows by gravity; basement waste is collected in sump pits and pumped out. The system uses UPVC soundproof piping throughout for quiet operation, with all stacks vented to roof level to maintain trap seals and prevent odour entry.

6.1 · Flow Path — How Drainage Works
STEP 1
FIXTURE DISCHARGE — Wastewater generated from WCs, showers, basins, floor drains, bathtubs, laundries and kitchens. Each point fitted with P-trap, bottle trap or multi-floor trap to maintain water seal and prevent odours.
STEP 2
FLOW SEGREGATION — Soil pipes (SP) receive discharge from WCs only. Waste pipes (WP) receive all other wastewater. Both systems independently vented through dedicated stacks to roof-level cowls.
STEP 3
VERTICAL CONVEYANCE — Wastewater from First Floor, Ground Floor and Roof flows vertically down through internal shafts via soil and waste stacks. Horizontal branches connect each fixture to the stacks.
STEP 4
GROUND FLOOR COLLECTION — All soil and waste lines terminate at external gully traps on the Ground Floor. Flow continues to external manholes and joins the main network.
STEP 5
BASEMENT COLLECTION — Basement wastewater flows by gravity into three sump pits (SLDP-01, SLDP-02, SLDP-03). Duplex submersible pumps automatically pump the waste up to a pressure break chamber, then by gravity to the septic tank.
STEP 6
FINAL DISCHARGE — All manholes converge to the main 102 m³ underground septic tank. Effluent from the septic tank is directed to the municipal sewer network when operating level is reached.

07 Pressurized Sump Pit Drainage System

Since the Basement sits below the main drainage network, wastewater cannot flow out by gravity. Instead, three pressurized sump pit stations — SLDP-01, SLDP-02, and SLDP-03 — collect the basement drainage and pump it upward through dedicated discharge lines. Each station is equipped with two pumps in duty/standby configuration, four-level float switch control, and a local control panel with full alarm indication.

08 Rain Water Drainage System

The rain water system collects storm water from all roof levels, balconies, and the ground floor perimeter, then discharges it through two independent duplex pump stations. The entire collection system operates on gravity — no pumping is required from roof to ground. Only at Ground Floor level do two sump pits (front and rear) collect the combined flow and pump it to the main septic tank and municipal drainage network.

11 Water Supply Contingency Operation

The water supply system has 7 defined contingency modes for use when equipment fails or requires maintenance. 52 isolation and control valves (GV-01 through GV-52) in the MEP service corridor allow the system to be reconfigured to maintain water supply in virtually any failure scenario. The full valve matrix is documented in the companion document: Water Supply System Contingency Plan — Part 2 (Valve Matrix & System Diagrams).

ModeScenario / UseKey Change
MODE AIrrigation pump failure or softener malfunctionBooster pumps draw directly from main tank — no softener
MODE BBooster pump failureIrrigation pumps supply building directly — no softener

12 System Integration & Controls

All plumbing systems in CEO Villa are interconnected and operate as one integrated water cycle. Understanding the relationship between systems helps the FM team manage the building effectively:

VFD-controlled booster pumps maintain constant 3.5-4.5 bar pressure regardless of how many fixtures are running simultaneously.
Pressure Reducing Valves (PRVs) on each floor independently regulate pressure to 3.5 bar, protecting delicate fixtures and mixers.
Float valves in both storage tanks prevent overflow and automatically stop pumps when tanks are full.
Hot water circulation pumps and thermal balancing valves ensure equal hot water temperature at every fixture — first floor to basement.
CALEFFI thermal disinfection and UV sterilization work together to provide a multi-barrier approach to microbiological water safety.
All basement sump pits (3 sewage + 2 rainwater = 5 total) operate fully automatically via float switches — no manual intervention needed during normal operation.
Rainwater system and sanitary drainage are completely separate networks that converge only at the main septic tank.
Chilled shower system operates as a standalone closed loop completely independent from the main cold-water dis tribution system.

1. SYSTEM OVERVIEW

This document defines the complete Sequence of Operation for the Rain Water Drainage System installed at CEO Villa, IHCC Project 10144, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. The system is a gravity-fed multi-level drainage network that collects rainfall from roof levels, terraces, and ground floor external areas, and discharges collected water via duplex submersible sump pump sets.

1.1 System Scope

The rain water drainage system at CEO Villa covers multiple collection levels across the building. At the highest level, the Upper Roof Terrace is drained by Saudi Cast stainless steel Linear Recessed Drains (Model FG 7840 GC) and supplemented by dome-type roof drains (Model FD 4160 NB). The two Lift Lobby Roofs serving Elevator-01 and Elevator-02 are equipped with Parapet Scupper Drains (Model FD 4020 NB, Cast Iron and SS, 110mm).

At First Floor level, three balconies are each fitted with Saudi Cast stainless steel Linear Recessed Drains (Model FG 7840 GC). These serve the Master Bathroom Balcony, the Master Bedroom Balcony, and the Guest Room (Bed Room #3) Balcony. Rain water from these balconies drains via vertical UPVC pipes embedded in the outside walls of the villa and discharges at Ground Floor level through Down Spot Nozzles.

The Lower Roof (MEP Equipment Area) receives the combined gravity flow from the Upper Roof and both Lift Lobby Roofs. It is equipped with fifteen Scupper Drains (Model FD 4100 G, Ductile Iron, 110mm) and discharges water further down through Down Spot Nozzles to Ground Floor via a UPVC Class-5 pipe riser network (SAPPCO KSA, 110mm).

At Ground Floor, the complete external perimeter is served by a BG-FILCOTEN Linear Concrete Drain network (Model EN W 100, HDP and SS, 100mm). The Ground Floor drainage is divided into two zones: the front side network drains to Sump-Pit-05 and the rear side network drains to Sump-Pit-06. Each sump pit houses a Duplex submersible pump set (Grundfos SEG-40-15-2-60G) controlled by a Schneider Electric NSYCNR panel in the Basement MEP Service Corridor.

1.2 Design Basis

The entire rain water drainage system is designed on a gravity-fed principle. No pumping is required at roof or first floor level — all water moves by natural slope and gravity from the point of collection down to Ground Floor. First Floor balcony water travels through vertical pipes embedded in the outside villa walls and exits at Ground Floor through Down Spot Nozzles.

At Ground Floor, the drainage network is divided into two independent zones. The front side collects into Sump-Pit-05 and the rear side collects into Sump-Pit-06. Each pit is served by a Duplex pump set operating on a Lead/Lag auto-alternating configuration, controlled entirely by float switches. No manual valve operation is required during normal rainfall events.

4. FLOAT SWITCH LEVEL CONTROL LOGIC

Each sump pit is equipped with four HANZ HANZT-5 float switches (DC 24V) operating at set elevations. The control panel (Schneider NSYCNR) reads all float switch signals and executes pump commands automatically. The same logic applies to both Sump-Pit-05 (SLDP-05) and Sump-Pit-06 (SLDP-06).

FLOAT SWITCH TAG ACTION DESCRIPTION
FS-01FV-01DRY RUN STOP / CUT-OFFFloat moves DOWN — lowest level. Both pumps STOP. Dry-run protection activated. Pumps cannot restart until FS-02 rises.
FS-02FV-02PUMP 1 START (LEAD)Float moves UP — water level rising. Duty pump (Lead Pump) starts automatically. Panel alternates lead pump after each cycle.
FS-03FV-03PUMP 2 START (LAG)Float moves UP — water level still rising with Pump 1 running. Standby pump (Lag Pump) starts — both pumps run simultaneously.
FS-04FV-04HIGH LEVEL ALARMFloat moves UP — critical high level. High level alarm activates (audible + visual). Both pumps already running. Requires immediate investigation.
4.1 Float Switch Elevation Notes

FS-01 is positioned at the lowest elevation, just above the pump intake — dry-run protection, cuts both pumps if level drops below safe threshold. FS-02 is set above FS-01 — minimum level to start Lead pump. FS-03 is positioned above FS-02 — activates when inflow exceeds Lead pump capacity, triggers Lag pump. FS-04 is at the highest position — critical overflow prevention level, activates high level alarm. The exact vertical spacing shall be confirmed with the panel commissioning engineer during system commissioning.

5. DETAILED SEQUENCE OF OPERATION
5.1 System Start-Up (Power ON — Normal Condition)

On initial power-up, the main supply of 380V, 3-Phase, 60Hz is confirmed to both control panels. The Schneider NSYCNR panels energize and perform a self-check. All four float switch inputs are read and the initial condition is assumed dry (FS-01 in the down position). Both pumps in each pit remain in standby mode. The panel alternation memory initializes with Pump-1 designated as the Lead pump for the first cycle. The system is now ready and waiting for a rainfall event.

5.2 Rainfall Event — Normal Rain (Single Pump Sufficient)
Stage 1 — Collection at Upper and First Floor Levels

When rainfall begins, water collects simultaneously across multiple levels. On the Upper Roof Terrace, water is collected by the Saudi Cast FG 7840 GC Linear Recessed Drains (lengths: 8570mm, 3950mm, 1900mm) and five Dome Deep Roof Drains (FD 4160 NB, 110mm). This water flows by gravity through the UPVC Class-5 110mm downpipe riser to the Lower Roof MEP Equipment Area. Simultaneously, the Parapet Scupper Drains on both Lift Lobby Roofs convey rainfall by gravity via UPVC Class-5 downpipes to the same Lower Roof level. At First Floor, all three balcony linear drains collect rainfall independently and flow into vertical UPVC pipes embedded in the outside villa walls, discharging at Ground Floor through Down Spot Nozzles.

Stage 2 — Lower Roof Collection and Discharge

The Lower Roof MEP Equipment Area receives the combined inflow from the Upper Roof and both Lift Lobby Roofs. The fifteen Scupper Drains (FD 4100 G, Ductile Iron, 110mm) collect standing water. Water is discharged to Ground Floor through Down Spot Nozzles: three units FD 8044 NB (110mm Bronze) carry Terrace path flow, and two units FD 8043 NB (75mm Bronze) carry Lift Lobby flow. The UPVC Class-5 riser also conveys water down to twelve Down Spot Nozzles (FD 8044 NB, 110mm) mounted on Ground Floor outdoor covered area walls.

Stage 3 — Ground Floor Collection — All Sources Converge

At Ground Floor, rain water from all drainage sources converges into the BG-FILCOTEN Linear Concrete Drain network (EN W 100, HDP and SS, 100mm) running around the full villa perimeter. The front side perimeter network directs water by gravity to Sump-Pit-05. The rear side network, including the Outdoor Powder Room discharge, directs to Sump-Pit-06.

Stage 4 — Sump Pit Filling and Pump Activation

As water enters the sump pit, the level rises. When the level reaches FS-01 (FV-01), the dry-run cut-off condition clears. When the level reaches FS-02 (FV-02), the float activates and the Schneider NSYCNR panel immediately starts the Lead pump — Grundfos SEG-40-15-2-60G — on 380V, 3-Phase, 60Hz. The pump draws water at 4.1 L/s and discharges through the CPVC 2" pipe, ITAP brass check valve (174 PSI rated), and FABCO CPVC ball valve to the designated discharge point. If inflow is lower than pump capacity, the level drops, FS-02 falls, and the Lead pump stops automatically.

Stage 5 — Lead Pump Stop and Auto-Alternation

After the Lead pump completes a cycle and stops, the control panel records the event. On the next FS-02 activation, the panel automatically designates Pump-2 as the new Lead pump and Pump-1 becomes Lag. This alternation continues with every completed cycle, ensuring equal running hours and uniform wear across both pumps.

5.3 Heavy Rainfall — Dual Pump Operation

During intense rainfall, when inflow exceeds single pump capacity, the water level continues to rise even with the Lead pump running. Once FS-03 (FV-03) activates, the panel immediately starts the Lag pump — both pumps operate simultaneously at a combined discharge rate of 8.2 L/s. As the combined pumping effort reduces the water level, FS-03 falls first and the Lag pump stops. The Lead pump continues running until FS-02 falls, then stops. System returns to standby.

5.4 High Level Alarm — Critical Condition

If the water level reaches FS-04 (FV-04) while both pumps are already running, a critical condition is indicated. The panel activates the high level alarm — audible buzzer and visual indicator light. If integrated with BMS, the alarm signal is transmitted to the central monitoring station. Immediate on-site investigation is required. Likely causes: pump failure, blocked/closed discharge valve, or extreme rainfall exceeding combined pump capacity. The maintenance team must verify both pumps are operating, confirm all discharge valves are fully open, inspect discharge line for blockage, and check all float switches.

5.5 Dry Run Protection — Low Level Cut-Off

If the water level inside the pit drops below FS-01 (FV-01) while a pump is running, dry-run protection activates immediately — both pumps stop to prevent damage to pump mechanical seal and motor windings. Pumps cannot restart until the level rises and FS-02 triggers. If FS-01 activates frequently, inspect float switch position, check pit inlet pipe for restriction, and verify ball valve on discharge line is not partially closed.

7. MODES OF OPERATION
7.1 AUTO Mode — Normal Operation

AUTO mode is selected via the selector switch on the panel face and is the normal operating condition at all times. All pump start/stop commands are governed exclusively by the float switches FS-01 through FS-04. Auto-alternation is active. High level alarm is fully active. Both panels must remain in AUTO mode during normal building operation and throughout any rainfall event.

7.2 MANUAL Mode — Maintenance and Testing

MANUAL mode is for commissioning, maintenance, and testing only. The operator can start or stop each pump individually. Float switch control is completely bypassed. High level alarm remains active. After any maintenance or test activity, the operator must immediately return the panel to AUTO mode.

7.3 OFF Mode

OFF mode disables both pumps entirely. Used only when maintenance work is carried out inside the sump pit or on the discharge pipework. Before selecting OFF mode and entering the pit, the operator must isolate power at the panel MCB and apply a lockout/tagout device. A valid confined space entry permit is required before any person enters the pit.

8. PUMP REMOVAL FOR MAINTENANCE

Each sump pit is equipped with guide rails and a stainless steel chain to facilitate pump removal without pit entry.

1.Switch control panel to OFF mode — isolate power at MCB
2.Obtain confined space permit if pit entry is required for any reason
3.Disconnect pump power cable at the junction box above pit — lock out / tag out
4.Uncouple discharge connection at the quick-release coupling above pit slab level
5.Attach lifting equipment (chain block or hoist) to the SS chain on the pump
6.Pull pump vertically upward along guide rails — do not tilt or force
7.Place pump on maintenance area for inspection, cleaning, or replacement
8.Reinstall in reverse order — confirm pump is fully seated on guide rail base
9.Reconnect discharge coupling and power cable
10.Return panel to AUTO mode — test pump operation with manual start before leaving site
9. ROUTINE MAINTENANCE REQUIREMENTS
9.1 Monthly Checks

Visually inspect both sump pits for debris — clean if required. Confirm both control panels are in AUTO mode. Test each pump individually in MANUAL mode — confirm flow from discharge point. Check all four float switches in each pit for free movement. Inspect CPVC discharge pipes and fittings for leakage. Verify high level alarm by manually lifting the FS-04 float and confirming alarm activates on the panel.

9.2 Quarterly Checks

Remove and clean all linear drain grates at Ground Floor, Lower Roof, and Upper Roof levels. Inspect and clear all Down Spot Nozzles of any blockage. Test pump auto-alternation — confirm the panel designates a different Lead pump after each cycle. Inspect guide rails inside both pits and lubricate; examine stainless steel lifting chains for corrosion or wear. Confirm ITAP check valves operate correctly with no backflow, and FABCO ball valves are fully open.

9.3 Annual Checks

Pull both pumps from their respective pits using guide rail and stainless steel chain system. Clean and inspect pump impellers and volutes for wear or blockage. Perform megger test on each motor winding — record insulation resistance values for trend monitoring. Replace float switches showing sluggish or erratic response. Check and clean UPVC riser pipes — inspect all joints for deterioration. Confirm BG-FILCOTEN linear drain channel sections are intact and correctly seated. Fully commission both control panels — test all interlocks, alternation logic, and alarm outputs.

10. ALARM SUMMARY
ALARM TRIGGER PUMP STATUS ACTION REQUIRED
High Level AlarmFS-04 (FV-04) activatedBoth pumps runningImmediate investigation — check pumps, discharge line, valves, float switches
Dry Run Cut-OffFS-01 (FV-01) falls — low levelBoth pumps STOPCheck water level — inspect float switch — check pit inlet
Pump FaultPump overload / motor tripAffected pump stopsCheck MCB / overload relay — inspect motor — reset after fault resolved
Power FailureSupply to panel lostBoth pumps stopRestore power — check MCB at panel and DB — check 3-phase supply
11. SAFETY PRECAUTIONS
⚠ CONFINED SPACE ENTRY — PERMIT REQUIRED

Both sump pits are classified as confined spaces. Entry requires a valid confined space permit issued by the site safety officer. Before any pit entry or pump maintenance, the control panel must be switched to OFF mode and power isolated at the MCB with a lockout/tagout device applied.

A calibrated gas detector must be used to check for toxic or oxygen-deficient atmosphere before entry. Float switches must never be overridden or bypassed during normal operation — this removes the only level protection for the pumps. The high level alarm must never be silenced without a physical investigation of the cause.

All electrical work on control panels or pump power circuits must be carried out only by a qualified and licensed electrician. Before restoring pump operation after any maintenance, confirm the discharge point is clear and unobstructed and all isolation valves are fully open.

Water Hardness Treatment — Normal Service Operation
1
Raw Water Entry (2–3 bar inlet)

Post-sediment and carbon filtered water enters Clack WS1 valve inlet.

2
Resin Bed Flow (Downward)

Water flows downward through 4 cu.ft of cation-exchange resin bed.

3
Ion Exchange (Continuous)

Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions attract to resin surface; Na⁺ ions release into solution. Hardness reduced from 20–30 GPG to <1 GPG.

4
Softened Water Exit (Continuous)

Treated water passes through Clack WS1 outlet to treated water storage tank at 20 GPM.

Automatic Regeneration Cycle — 4 Stages

Triggered when preset capacity is reached (typically 20,000–30,000 gallons). Total cycle time: approximately 60 minutes.

1
Backwash (~5 min)

Water flow reversed upward through resin bed, loosening media and dislodging accumulated sediment. Waste discharged through dedicated backwash drain line.

2
Brine Draw & Slow Rinse (~30 min)

Saturated brine from brine tank introduced downward through resin bed. High sodium displaces hardness ions (Ca²⁺, Mg²⁺) through ion exchange. Waste brine discharged through backwash drain.

3
Fast Rinse (~10 min)

Fresh treated water flushes remaining brine and residual hardness ions downward through resin bed. Discharged through backwash drain. Resin clean and fully regenerated.

4
Brine Tank Refill (~10 min)

Fresh water automatically refills brine tank, dissolving salt to form saturated brine for next cycle. Float valve regulates level and prevents overfilling.

Thermal Disinfection Cycle — Legionella Control

Legionella pneumophila grows optimally at 20–45°C. Periodic heating to 60–80°C kills bacteria and prevents colonization. Disinfection set at 65°C, 30 minutes duration, weekly (typically every Sunday 2–4 AM).

1
Pre-Disinfection Check (5 min)

Verifies heater temperature >60°C, cold water availability, and adequate circulation flow. Auto-aborts if conditions not met.

2
Ramp-Up Phase (5–10 min)

Mixing valve increases hot water proportion, gradually raising temperature toward 65°C disinfection setpoint. Controlled ramp prevents thermal shock.

3
Disinfection Holding (20–60 min (typically 30))

Valve maintains stable 65°C throughout villa hot water piping. Hot water circulates through all branches and dead legs. If temperature deviates >3°C, cycle aborts automatically.

4
Cool-Down Phase (10–15 min)

Hot water proportion gradually decreases, returning mixed water temperature smoothly to 42–48°C normal operating range.

5
Return to Normal (—)

Valve returns to normal mixing mode at 42–48°C. System fully available for villa use.

SEQUENCE OF OPERATION — SANITARY DRAINAGE SYSTEM
CEO VILLA  ·  PROJECT CODE: 10144  ·  IHCC JEDDAH KSA  ·  7 SECTIONS
01 SYSTEM OVERVIEW

The drainage and sewerage system of the CEO Villa ensures hygienic and efficient removal of wastewater and rainwater from all wet facilities. It serves 43 drainage points including toilets, baths, laundries, kitchens, and parking areas across basement, ground, first floor, and roof levels.

The system operates through gravity flow for upper floors and pressurized discharge from basement sump pits — all vented and interconnected to the main septic tank and municipality sewer line.

02 GENERAL DESIGN FEATURES
FEATURESPECIFICATION
Piping MaterialUPVC (soundproof type) throughout the building
Joints — Non-PressurizedRubber push-fit joints
Joints — PressurizedSolvent joints (Class-5 pipes and fittings)
VentilationAll soil and waste stacks extended to roof level with vent cowls
IdentificationAll piping tagged and labeled — standard color coding
Traps — Floor DrainsMulti-Floor Traps (MFT) with KESSEL Multi-Stop backflow preventers
Traps — Basins/SinksBottle traps under wash basins and sinks
Backflow ProtectionGully traps with non-return valves between internal systems and manholes
03 SEQUENCE OF OPERATION
1
Fixture Discharge

Wastewater generated from WCs, showers, wash basins, floor drains, bathtubs, laundries and kitchens. Each discharge point fitted with an appropriate trap (P-trap, bottle trap or multi-floor trap) to retain a water seal and prevent odor entry.

2
Flow Segregation

Soil Pipes (SP) receive discharge only from WCs. Waste Pipes (WP) receive discharge from floor drains, showers, sinks, laundry, kitchen and parking areas. Soil Vent Pipes (SVP) and Waste Vent Pipes (WVP) connected independently to their respective stacks — vented through roof-level cowls to maintain pressure equilibrium.

3
Vertical & Horizontal Conveyance

Wastewater from upper floors (roof, first and ground floors) flows vertically through shafts via soil and waste stacks. Horizontal branches connect fixtures to the main stacks via traps and cleanouts.

4
Flow Collection — Ground & Upper Floors

All soil and waste lines terminate into external gully traps on the ground floor. Flow continues from gully traps to external manholes connected to the main network.

5
Flow Collection — Basement

Basement-level wastewater gravitates into three sump pits (each 5.8 m³ capacity). Each pit has duplex submersible pumps operating alternately. When water reaches high level, lead pump starts automatically. Lag pump engages if required. Pumps discharge to pressurized break chambers, then by gravity to the main septic tank.

6
Ground Floor Rainwater & Surface Drainage

Two rainwater sump pits (front and rear, each 8 m³) collect runoff from linear drains and roof downpipes. Duplex submersible pumps transfer rainwater to the main septic tank and then to the municipality sewer network.

7
Final Discharge

All manholes converge to the main septic tank. Effluent from the septic tank is directed to the municipal sewer line once the operating level is reached.

02 FLOAT SWITCH SETTINGS & FUNCTIONS
FLOAT SWITCHLEVELHEIGHT FROM BASEFUNCTION
FS-01 — Low Level Shut-offLevel 1350mmStops ALL pumps & activates Low Level Alarm to protect pump from dry running
FS-02 — Pump 1 StartLevel 2500mmStarts Pump 1 in AUTO mode when water rises. Stops Pump 1 when water falls back.
FS-03 — Pump 2 StartLevel 3750mmStarts Pump 2 + activates High Alarm (in addition to Pump 1). Stops Pump 2 and silences alarm when water falls.
FS-04 — High Level AlarmLevel 41,200mmStops ALL pumps & activates audible and visual alarms — indicates risk of overflow.
03 AUTO MODE OPERATION
Normal Operation Sequence
1
Water Level Below FS-02 (< 500mm)

Both pumps remain OFF. System in standby.

2
Water Level Reaches FS-02 (500mm)

Pump 1 starts automatically. Water level begins to drop.

3
If Inflow Rate > Pump 1 Capacity

Water continues rising to FS-03 (750mm). Pump 2 starts automatically in parallel with Pump 1. Audible High Level Alarm activates.

4
Stopping Sequence

When water drops below FS-03 → Pump 2 stops + High Level Alarm stops. Pump 1 continues running until water drops below FS-01 (350mm) → Pump 1 stops.

5
Low Level Protection

If pump(s) continue running and water reaches FS-01 fall level — ALL pumps stop + Audible Low Level Alarm activates to prevent dry running.

Alternation Logic

The starting pump alternates between Pump 1 and Pump 2 each cycle to equalize wear and running time. In case of failure of the lead pump, the lag pump automatically starts when its float switch is triggered.

04 MANUAL MODE OPERATION

Operator can start either pump using the START push button regardless of float switch status. Pump runs until manually stopped. Low level protection is active only if wired in series with manual mode — otherwise operator must monitor visually.

05 SAFETY & ALARM FUNCTIONS
CONDITIONTRIGGERACTION
High Level AlarmFS-04 activated (1,200mm)Red HIGH LEVEL lamp illuminates + buzzer sounds + ALL pumps stop
Low Level AlarmFS-01 activated (350mm)Red LOW LEVEL lamp illuminates + all running pumps shut down (dry run protection)
Trip IndicatorMotor overload or faultRed TRIP lamp illuminates for affected pump
Mute ButtonManual pressSilences buzzer — visual alarms remain active until fault clears
06 ISOLATION & MAINTENANCE
  • Individual isolation valves allow removal of each pump without draining the pit
  • Check valves prevent backflow when pumps stop
  • Main discharge isolation valve allows full system shutdown for maintenance
07 TYPICAL OPERATIONAL CYCLE EXAMPLE
1
Water Level at 300mm

Both pumps OFF — below FS-02 threshold.

2
Water Rises to 500mm

FS-02 triggers → Pump 1 starts automatically.

3
Inflow Surpasses Pump 1 Capacity

Water rises to 750mm → FS-03 triggers → Pump 2 starts + High Level Alarm sounds.

4
Pumps Run Together

Level drops below 750mm → FS-03 resets → Pump 2 stops + alarm silences.

5
Pump 1 Continues

Level drops below 350mm → FS-01 resets → Pump 1 stops.

6
Emergency Condition

If water rises to 1,200mm at any time → FS-04 triggers → ALL pumps stop + alarm + buzzer.

02 SYSTEM OVERVIEW

The Cold/Chilled Water System provides two temperature options for shower usage at both the SPA Shower (Basement) and Master Shower (First Floor).

MODE 1: NORMAL COLD WATER
  • Standard municipal cold water (~25°C)
  • Mixed with hot water from heater
  • User controls temperature via shower mixer
MODE 2: CHILLED WATER
  • Chilled water from rooftop chiller (10°C)
  • Mixed with hot water from heater
  • Refreshing cold shower experience

06 OPERATIONAL PROCEDURES
SEQUENCE 1 — Starting Chilled Water System

(Switching from Normal Cold Mode to Chilled Mode)

1
ISOLATE NORMAL COLD WATER SUPPLY
  • At Roof (Master Shower Valve Station): Close GV-77
  • At Basement SPA Lobby: Close GV-72
  • Verification: Valve handles perpendicular to pipe
2
OPEN CHILLER ISOLATION VALVES
  • At Roof (Chiller Location): Open GV-76, GV-79, GV-82 (Fresh water supply)
  • Open GV-83 (Chilled water outlet)
  • Open GV-84 (Return line)
  • Verification: All valve handles parallel to pipe
3
OPEN CHILLED WATER SUPPLY TO SHOWERS
  • At Roof: Open GV-78 (Chilled water to Master Shower)
  • At Roof: Open GV-80 & GV-81 (Chilled water to SPA Shower)
  • At Basement: Open GV-71 (Chilled water to SPA Shower)
4
START CHILLER SYSTEM
  • Turn ON chiller main power switch at control panel
  • Duty circulation pump starts automatically
  • Fresh water fills 1,000L storage tank
  • Chiller compressor starts and cools water to 10°C
  • System reaches operating temperature in 15–20 minutes
5
SYSTEM VERIFICATION
  • Listen for circulation pump running
  • Check temperature display shows ~10°C
  • Verify chilled water at shower heads (test briefly)
  • Check for any leakage at all valve locations
✓ COMPLETION — Chilled Water Mode Active
  • Chilled water (10°C) available at both Master Shower and SPA Shower
  • All chiller isolation valves confirmed open
  • Normal cold water supply isolated at GV-77 and GV-72
SEQUENCE 2 — Stopping Chilled Water System

(Switching from Chilled Mode to Normal Cold Mode)

1
TURN OFF CHILLER
  • Turn OFF chiller main power switch
  • Compressor and pumps stop automatically
  • Wait 2–3 minutes for complete shutdown
2
CLOSE CHILLED WATER SUPPLY TO SHOWERS
  • At Roof: Close GV-78 & GV-79 (Chilled water to Master)
  • At Basement: Close GV-71 (Chilled water to SPA)
  • Alternative: Close GV-81 & GV-82 at Roof
3
CLOSE CHILLER ISOLATION VALVES
  • At Chiller: Close GV-84 (Return line)
  • Close GV-83 (Chilled water outlet)
  • Close GV-82 (Fresh water supply)
4
OPEN NORMAL COLD WATER SUPPLY
  • At Roof: Open GV-77 (Normal cold water to Master)
  • At Basement: Open GV-72 (Normal cold water to SPA)
5
SYSTEM VERIFICATION
  • Verify chiller completely shut down (no sounds)
  • Test normal cold water at shower heads
  • Verify hot water still available
✓ COMPLETION — Normal Cold Water Mode Active
  • Chiller safely isolated
  • Normal cold water supply restored at both showers
  • Hot water remains available throughout
07 AUTOMATIC CONTROL SEQUENCES
Temperature Control — When Chiller Operating
CONDITIONACTION
Duty circulation pumpRuns continuously — one pump always running
Temperature setpoint10°C outlet temperature
When Temperature > 10°CCompressor STARTS automatically — refrigeration cycle cools water
When Temperature = 10°CCompressor STOPS automatically — circulation pump continues running
During shower usageFresh water enters tank → chiller activates → maintains 10°C automatically
Storage Tank Function

1,000 litres of chilled water ready for instant delivery. When shower is used, fresh water enters and chiller activates. System automatically maintains 10°C during and after usage.

Pump Duty/Standby Operation
CONDITIONACTION
Normal operationPump #1 runs as Duty pump — Pump #2 on Standby
Duty pump failureStandby pump starts automatically — no interruption
Changeover eventAlarm indication on control panel
System continuityOperation continues without interruption
08 SAFETY INTERLOCKS & PROTECTIONS
PROTECTIONTRIGGERACTION
Low Water FlowCirculation stopsCompressor shuts down automatically to prevent freezing damage
High Pressure CutoffRefrigerant pressure exceeds limitCompressor stops — manual reset required
Low Pressure CutoffIndicates refrigerant leakCompressor stops — service required
Motor OverloadExcessive current drawProtects compressor and pump motors
Phase ProtectionPhase loss on 3-phase supplyPrevents operation — system shutdown
Thermal Overload (Pumps)Pump overheatingEach pump protected — automatic reset after cooling
⚠️ ALARM CONDITIONS
  • When any safety device trips: Visual/audible alarm on control panel
  • System shutdown — requires investigation and reset
  • Do NOT restart system until fault investigated by qualified technician
09 EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN PROCEDURE
⚠️ PERFORM EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN IF:
  • Major water leak detected
  • Electrical fault or sparking observed
  • Fire or smoke from equipment
  • Strong refrigerant odor detected
  • Unusual loud noise or vibration
  • Any safety concern
IMMEDIATE ACTIONS — Emergency Shutdown
1
Turn OFF Chiller
  • Turn OFF chiller main power switch immediately
2
Close Chiller Valves
  • Close all three chiller isolation valves (GV-82, GV-83, GV-84)
3
Electrical Hazard
  • If electrical hazard present: Turn OFF main electrical disconnect
4
Secure Area
  • Barricade area to prevent entry
  • Contact maintenance supervisor immediately
5
Fire / Refrigerant
  • Fire: Activate fire alarm and evacuate
  • Refrigerant leak: Evacuate area and ventilate
Restore Normal Water Supply After Emergency
  • At Master Shower (Roof): Follow Sequence 2 — Steps 3 and 4
  • At SPA Shower (Basement): Open GV-72 (Normal Cold Water)
  • Verify shower water service restored in Normal Cold Mode
⚠️ IMPORTANT
  • Do NOT restart system until fault investigated and corrected by qualified technician

01 PURPOSE AND SCOPE

This Contingency Operation Plan provides alternative operational modes for the water supply system to maintain continuous service during equipment failures, maintenance activities, or emergency situations. The plan covers valve operation procedures for 52 isolation and control valves (GV-01 through GV-52) located in the MEP service corridor.

⚠ IMPORTANT NOTE

Contingency plans are intended solely for emergency situations and are not designed for permanent operation. They do not represent full system performance. Return to normal operation as soon as repairs are completed.

Valve positions for each mode are documented in the companion document: Part 2 of 2 — Valve Matrix & System Diagrams (available in Contingency Plan Valve Matrix tab).

02 SYSTEM OVERVIEW
COMPONENTDESCRIPTION
Main Water Storage TankPrimary water source
Booster Pump SystemPressurizes water for building distribution
Irrigation Water Supply PumpsTransfer water to intermediate storage
Intermediate Storage TankBuffer storage for treated water
Water Softener PlantRemoves hardness from water
Hot Water Heaters (×2)Provide hot water for facilities
Distribution Network3-pipe system — Cold, Hot Supply, Hot Return
52 Isolation/Control ValvesEnable system reconfiguration (GV-01 to GV-52)
03 NORMAL OPERATION MODE

Under normal operating conditions, all system components function in their designed configuration:

  1. Water flows from main tank through irrigation pumps to intermediate storage tank
  2. Water passes through softener plant for treatment
  3. Booster pumps pressurize treated water for building distribution
  4. Cold water distributes through 63mm Ø main pipe to all 42 facilities
  5. Hot water system operates with both heaters functional
  6. Hot water recirculation maintains temperature throughout the building
  7. All isolation valves remain in their standard operational positions
04 CONTINGENCY OPERATION MODES

Seven contingency modes are defined. Each mode describes when to use it, how the system operates, and which valves must be changed.

A
MODE A — BOOSTER PUMPS ONLY
WITHOUT SOFTENER
APPLICATION

Irrigation pump failure or maintenance · Softener plant malfunction or regeneration · Intermediate storage tank issues

OPERATION

Booster pumps draw water directly from the main tank, bypassing irrigation pumps, intermediate storage tank, and softener plant. Untreated water supplies the building. Both water heaters remain functional.

CRITICAL VALVES
CLOSE:
● CLOSE GV-01● CLOSE GV-02● CLOSE GV-24● CLOSE GV-27● CLOSE GV-28● CLOSE GV-36● CLOSE GV-37● CLOSE GV-44● CLOSE GV-46● CLOSE GV-47● CLOSE GV-48● CLOSE GV-50● CLOSE GV-51
OPEN:
● OPEN GV-25 (bypass to booster pumps)● OPEN GV-40 (direct supply from main tank)
MAINTAIN OPEN:
◈ All distribution valves to facilities
◈ All heater supply and return valves (GV-17 through GV-23)
B
MODE B — IRRIGATION PUMPS ONLY
WITHOUT SOFTENER
APPLICATION

Booster pump failure or maintenance · Softener plant malfunction

OPERATION

Irrigation pumps draw water from main tank and supply directly to building, bypassing the softener plant and intermediate storage tank. Booster pumps are isolated. Untreated water supplies the building. Both water heaters remain functional.

CRITICAL VALVES
CLOSE:
● CLOSE GV-25● CLOSE GV-26● CLOSE GV-40● CLOSE GV-43● CLOSE GV-44● CLOSE GV-46
OPEN:
● OPEN GV-37 (irrigation pump discharge to distribution)
MAINTAIN OPEN:
◈ All distribution valves to facilities
◈ All heater supply and return valves
C
MODE C — BOOSTER PUMPS ONLY
WITH SOFTENER
APPLICATION

Irrigation pump failure · Intermediate storage tank issues · Softener plant operational (preferred mode when possible)

OPERATION

Booster pumps draw water directly from main tank, passing through the softener plant for treatment before distribution. Irrigation pumps and intermediate storage tank are bypassed. Treated water supplies the building. Both water heaters remain functional.

CRITICAL VALVES
CLOSE:
● CLOSE GV-01● CLOSE GV-24● CLOSE GV-27● CLOSE GV-28● CLOSE GV-36● CLOSE GV-37● CLOSE GV-43● CLOSE GV-44
OPEN:
● OPEN GV-40 (main tank to softener)● OPEN GV-25 (softener to booster pumps)
MAINTAIN OPEN:
◈ Softener inlet/outlet valves
◈ All distribution and heater valves
D
MODE D — IRRIGATION PUMPS ONLY
WITH SOFTENER
APPLICATION

Booster pump failure or maintenance · Intermediate storage tank issues · Softener plant operational

OPERATION

Irrigation pumps draw water from main tank and supply through the softener plant directly to building distribution, bypassing the intermediate storage tank and booster pumps. Treated water supplies the building. Both water heaters remain functional.

CRITICAL VALVES
CLOSE:
● CLOSE GV-24● CLOSE GV-27● CLOSE GV-28● CLOSE GV-36● CLOSE GV-40● CLOSE GV-43● CLOSE GV-44
OPEN:
● OPEN GV-01 (main tank to irrigation pumps)● OPEN GV-02 (main tank to irrigation pumps)● OPEN GV-37 (irrigation pump through softener to distribution)
MAINTAIN OPEN:
◈ Softener inlet/outlet valves
◈ All distribution and heater valves
E
MODE E — ISOLATING WATER HEATERS
HOT WATER SYSTEM
APPLICATION

Water heater failure, leak, or maintenance · Hot water system emergency · Heater repair or replacement required

OPERATION

All other systems operate according to the selected operational mode (A, B, C, or D), but both water heaters are bypassed. Only cold water is available throughout the building. Hot water supply and return lines are isolated.

CRITICAL VALVES
CLOSE:
● CLOSE GV-17● CLOSE GV-18● CLOSE GV-19 (heater isolation)● CLOSE GV-21● CLOSE GV-22● CLOSE GV-23 (TBV & return isolation)● CLOSE GV-46 (hot water supply to distribution)
OPEN:
MAINTAIN OPEN:
◈ Selected pump configuration valves (Mode A, B, C, or D)
◈ Cold water distribution valves
⚠️ No hot water will be available to any facility when heaters are isolated. Notify all building occupants before implementing this mode.
F
MODE F — ISOLATING THERMAL BALANCING VALVES
TBV MAINTENANCE
APPLICATION

Danfoss MCTV thermal balancing valve maintenance · Hot water return line balancing issues · TBV replacement required

OPERATION

Hot water circulation continues without balancing valve control. This may result in uneven temperature distribution and reduced efficiency. Return to normal operation as soon as possible.

CRITICAL VALVES
CLOSE:
● CLOSE GV-20 (TBV isolation)
OPEN:
MAINTAIN OPEN:
◈ All other valves in normal or selected contingency positions
G
MODE G — MAIN TANK DRAIN / EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN
COMPLETE SHUTDOWN
APPLICATION

Main tank maintenance or inspection · System contamination requiring full drainage · Emergency shutdown of entire water supply system · Major leak or system failure

OPERATION

COMPLETE SYSTEM SHUTDOWN. All water supply to the building is interrupted. This mode should only be used in genuine emergencies or planned maintenance with advance notification.

CRITICAL VALVES
CLOSE:

06 SWITCHING PROCEDURES
6.1 General Safety Requirements
  • Only authorized maintenance personnel may operate system valves
  • Notify building management before switching operational modes
  • Document all valve position changes in the maintenance log
  • Verify system pressure before and after switching
  • Monitor for leaks after valve operations
  • Keep this contingency plan accessible in the MEP room at all times
6.2 Switching from Normal to Contingency Mode
  1. Identify the required contingency mode based on the failure/maintenance needs
  2. Refer to Part 2 of 2 — Valve Operation Matrix for specific valve positions
  3. De-energize affected pumps before closing their isolation valves
  4. Close valves marked RED (CLOSE) in the target contingency mode column
  5. Open valves marked GREEN (OPEN) in the target contingency mode column
  6. Energize pumps required for the new operational mode
  7. Verify water flow and pressure at representative fixtures
  8. Monitor system for 15–30 minutes to ensure stable operation
  9. Document mode change with date, time, reason, and operator name
  10. Post notice in MEP room indicating current operational mode
6.3 Returning to Normal Operation
  1. Verify that all repairs/maintenance are complete and tested
  2. De-energize pumps in contingency configuration
  3. Restore all valves to NORMAL operation positions (refer to Part 2 of 2)
  4. Follow the valve sequence carefully to avoid water hammer
  5. Energize pumps in their normal operational sequence
  6. Verify system pressure and flow at all zones
  7. Check for any leaks at valve stems or connections
  8. Test hot water availability if heaters were isolated
  9. Monitor system for 1 hour to ensure stable operation
  10. Document return to normal operation in maintenance log
  11. Remove contingency mode notice from MEP room
07 EMERGENCY RESPONSE
7.1
Major Water Leak
  • Immediately close the nearest isolation valve(s) to the leak
  • If leak cannot be isolated, implement MODE G (Main Tank Drain)
  • De-energize all affected pumps
  • Notify building management and emergency contacts
  • Drain affected sections if necessary
  • Do not restore water supply until repairs are verified
7.2
Complete Power Failure
  • All pumps will stop automatically
  • Water supply will continue from system pressure until depleted
  • Do not attempt to manually operate electric pumps
  • When power is restored, verify pump motor rotation direction
  • Gradually restart pumps one at a time
  • Check for air locks and vent if necessary
7.3
Water Quality Issues
  • If contamination detected, close GV-01 and GV-02 immediately
  • Isolate softener plant if contamination source is suspected there
  • Drain affected sections completely
  • Flush system with clean water before resuming service
  • Test water quality before returning to normal operation
  • Consider temporary bottled water supply for drinking/cooking

1. SYSTEM DESCRIPTION

The Rain Water Drainage System at CEO Villa consists of two reinforced concrete sump pits installed at Ground Floor level for collection and automatic discharge of rainwater collected from all roof levels, first floor balconies, security room, outdoor powder room, and ground floor perimeter drain networks.

Sump Pit-05 is located at the Front Side (West Side) of the Villa and receives rainwater from the front perimeter drain network. Sump Pit-06 is located at the Rear Side (East Side) of the Villa and receives rainwater from the rear perimeter drain network including the Outdoor Powder Room.

Each sump pit is equipped with duplex submersible pump sets (Grundfos SEG-40-15-2-60G) operating in Duty/Standby auto-alternating mode for automatic rainwater discharge. Both pump control panels (Schneider Electric NSYCNR) are installed inside the Basement MEP Service Corridor. Each pit contains the following:

SUMP PIT-05 — FRONT (WEST)
✔ Two (2) Grundfos Submersible Pumps
✔ Four (4) HANZ Float Switches (FS-01 to FS-04)
✔ Stainless Steel Guide Rails
✔ Stainless Steel Lifting Chains
✔ Duplex Pump Control Panel (NSYCNR)
✔ High Level Alarm System (FS-04)
SUMP PIT-06 — REAR (EAST)
✔ Two (2) Grundfos Submersible Pumps
✔ Four (4) HANZ Float Switches (FS-01 to FS-04)
✔ Stainless Steel Guide Rails

4. FLOAT SWITCH OPERATION LOGIC

Each sump pit contains four HANZ HANZT-5 float switches positioned at set elevations. The Schneider NSYCNR control panel reads all float switch signals and executes pump commands automatically. The same logic applies identically to both Sump-Pit-05 and Sump-Pit-06.

Float Switch Tag Trigger Movement System Action
FS-01 FV-01 Dry Run / Low Level ↓ Move DOWN BOTH PUMPS STOP immediately. Dry-run protection activated. Pumps cannot restart until FS-02 rises.
FS-02 FV-02 Water Level Rising — Normal ↑ Move UP DUTY PUMP (Lead) STARTS automatically. RUN indication light illuminates on panel.
FS-03 FV-03 Level Rising — Duty Pump Insufficient ↑ Move UP STANDBY PUMP STARTS — both pumps run simultaneously. Combined discharge 8.2 L/s.
FS-04 FV-04 CRITICAL HIGH LEVEL ↑ Move UP HIGH LEVEL ALARM activates — audible + visual. Both pumps run. BMS signal transmitted. IMMEDIATE investigation required.

5. DETAILED SEQUENCE OF OPERATION
Step Condition / Trigger System Action
NORMAL OPERATING CONDITION — AUTO MODE
1Panel Power ONMain power supply 380V-3Ph-60Hz confirmed. Control panels energise. POWER indicator (White) illuminates. All float switch inputs read — initial state assumed dry with FS-01 down. Both pumps standby.
2A-O-H in AUTO positionBoth pumps placed in AUTO mode via A-O-H selector switches. L-O-R set to LOCAL or REMOTE as required. System ready — waiting for rainfall event.
FS-01 — DRY RUN PROTECTION (Low Level Cut-Off)
3FS-01 drops — low levelBOTH PUMPS STOP immediately. Dry-run protection activated to prevent pump seal and motor damage. Pumps cannot restart until FS-02 rises again.
FS-02 — DUTY PUMP START (Normal Rain)
4FS-02 activates — water risingControl panel receives signal from FV-02. DUTY (Lead) PUMP starts automatically — Grundfos SEG-40-15-2-60G energizes on 380V-3Ph-60Hz. RUN indicator illuminates. Pump discharges at 4.1 L/s through CPVC 2" pipe — ITAP check valve — FABCO ball valve — discharge point.
5Water level drops — FS-02 fallsDuty pump stops automatically. Panel records completed cycle. On next FS-02 activation, panel alternates — Pump-2 becomes Lead. Auto-alternation ensures equal runtime on both pumps.
FS-03 — STANDBY PUMP START (Heavy Rain — Dual Pump Operation)
6FS-03 activates — level still risingInflow exceeds duty pump capacity. FV-03 activates — STANDBY (Lag) PUMP starts automatically. Both pumps operate simultaneously. Combined discharge rate: 2 × 4.1 L/s = 8.2 L/s. Both RUN indicators illuminate.
7Level drops — FS-03 then FS-02 fallAs combined pumping reduces level, FS-03 falls first — Standby pump stops. Level continues falling — FS-02 falls — Duty pump stops. System returns to standby.
FS-04 — CRITICAL HIGH LEVEL ALARM
8FS-04 activates — critical levelHIGH LEVEL ALARM activates — audible buzzer and amber indicator lamp on panel illuminate. Both pumps already running. BMS alarm signal transmitted. IMMEDIATE site investigation required — check pump operation, discharge valve position, pipe blockage, and float switch condition.
PUMP TRIP CONDITION
9Overload / Overcurrent / Phase failureAffected pump stops immediately. TRIP indicator (Red) illuminates for that pump. Other pump continues in operation if auto — single pump operation mode. Fault must be investigated, rectified, and ALARM RESET pressed before pump returns to service.
MANUAL OPERATION (A-O-H in HAND position)
10A-O-H set to HANDFloat switch control bypassed. Operator starts/stops pump manually via push buttons. For testing and maintenance only. HIGH LEVEL alarm remains active. Return selector to AUTO immediately after completing work.
REMOTE OPERATION (L-O-R in REMOTE position)
11L-O-R set to REMOTEPump control transferred to BMS/PLC system. Local panel push buttons disabled in remote mode. Used when building automation system is managing pump operation centrally.
ALARM RESET PROCEDURE
12After fault rectificationIdentify and rectify the cause of the alarm. Confirm pit water level is safe. Confirm pump condition is satisfactory. Press ALARM RESET push button on panel face. Confirm indicators return to normal state. Return A-O-H to AUTO mode.
6. DUPLEX PUMP CONTROL PANEL — COMPONENTS & FUNCTIONS

The Schneider Electric NSYCNR Duplex Pump Control Panel is located in the Basement MEP Service Corridor. The panel face layout is shown below, followed by a description of each component and its function.

Figure 3 — Duplex Pump Control Panel Face Layout (Schneider NSYCNR)
Component Indication / Colour Function / Description
HIGH LEVEL IndicatorAmber / OrangeIlluminates when water level reaches FS-04 (FV-04) critical high-high level. Connected to audible alarm and BMS monitoring system.
POWER IndicatorWhiteConfirms the control panel is energised and control power supply is healthy. Must be ON at all times during normal operation.
PUMP NO.1 — RUNGreen / TealConfirms Pump No.1 is running via contactor/VFD feedback signal. Illuminates when duty pump is operating.
PUMP NO.1 — TRIPRedIlluminates when Pump No.1 has tripped due to overload, overcurrent, thermal protection activation, or phase failure.
PUMP NO.2 — RUNGreen / TealConfirms Pump No.2 is operating. Illuminates when standby pump is running — either in Auto or Manual mode.
PUMP NO.2 — TRIPRedIlluminates when Pump No.2 has tripped. Investigate cause before attempting reset.
A-O-H SelectorA = AUTO O = OFF H = HANDAUTO — float switch control (normal mode). OFF — pump disabled. HAND — manual operation for maintenance and testing. Return to AUTO immediately after use.
ALARM RESET ButtonBlack Push ButtonResets active alarms after the fault condition has been rectified. Do not reset without first identifying and resolving the cause of the alarm.
L-O-R SelectorL = LOCAL O = OFF R = REMOTELOCAL — control from panel push buttons. OFF — control disabled. REMOTE — control via BMS or PLC system. Keep in LOCAL unless BMS remote control is active and commissioned.
7. PUMP REMOVAL & MAINTENANCE FEATURES

Each sump pit is equipped with Stainless Steel Guide Rails and Stainless Steel Lifting Chains to allow safe removal and reinstallation of both submersible pumps without requiring personnel to enter the sump pit.

To remove a pump, the technician switches the relevant pump to OFF mode, isolates power at the panel MCB, disconnects the pump discharge coupling and power cable junction box above pit level, attaches a chain block or hoist to the SS lifting chain, and pulls the pump vertically upward along the guide rails. The pump is then placed on the maintenance area for inspection or replacement. Reinstallation follows the reverse procedure. After reinstallation, the pump must be tested in MANUAL mode before returning to AUTO mode.

⚠ CONFINED SPACE — MANDATORY SAFETY REQUIREMENTS

Both sump pits are classified as confined spaces. A valid confined space entry permit and gas detection check are mandatory before any person enters the pit for any reason.

8. SYSTEM OPERATION SUMMARY

The Rain Water Submersible Pump System is designed for fully automatic, unattended operation through float switch level control logic. The duplex pump arrangement provides operational redundancy, high-level overflow protection, and maintenance flexibility through auto-alternation of the duty and standby pumps after each completed cycle.
